main_text.p: Hymettus mons Atticæ, vbi optimæ apes.

p.l: Quàm vultus, oculósque tuos, ô dulcior illo
Melle, quod in ceris Attica ponit apis.
Qua Tritonide fertiles Athenas
Vnctis Bœotica prouocas trapetis.
Vertice de summo semper florentis Hymetti
Lutea mane videt, pulsis Aurora tenebris.
Proximus hinc Butes Atthis dies ab oris:
Innumeras nam claudit apes, longaque superbus
Fuscat nube diem dum plenas nectare cellas
Pandit, & in dulcem reges dimittit Hymeton.

main_text.head: Megara regio Atticæ vicina, & Peloponnefo.

p.l: Liquerat Ortygiam, Megaréaque, Pantagiénque,
Quáque Simetheas accipit æquor aquas.
—viuo prætereuhor ostia saxo
Pantagia, Megarósque sinus, Tapsúmque iacentem.

main_text.head: Achaia Græciæ regio Megaram excipit, in qua est Corinthus oppidum.
Corinthus.

p.l: Laudabunt alij claram Rhodon, aut Mytelenem,
Aut Ephesum, bimarisve Corinthi Mœnia.
Orchomenósque ferax, & nobilis are Corinthos.
p.note: Ouid.Meta. lib.6. Ouid.Trist. lib.1. Idem lib.3.
p.l: Illa Corinthiacis primum mihi cognita Cenchris
Fida manet trepida dúxque, comésque fuga.
Non ego Medea vellem frenare Dracones:
Quos habuit fugiens arce Corinthe tua.
—despicias tu
Forsitan imbelles Rhodios, vnáámq; Corinthum?

page.notes: Marginal notes in the right margin are small italic citations; the Greek words are rendered as printed in Latin letters where the scan is unclear. Doubtful readings: "Atthis" and "Tapsus" in the notes; "Tapsúmque" and "Megarósque" in the verse; "vnáámq;" possibly "vnàmque".
